evals.prompt: Show me the brain by lobe so I can rotate it and name each one: the four lobes, the insula, the cerebellum and the brainstem. One HTML file I can open offline, light theme.
evals.expected_output: The response takes the 3D route (it says so, and says it takes minutes, not an Epic) with BodyParts3D as the atlas. It runs scripts/atlas.mjs bp3d --find for each requested name, writes a truth.mjs whose PARTS have atlas ids and the atlas's own names (right and left lobes as one row with two ids; the brainstem as midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata, or as one brainstem mesh if the user wanted one part, and says which), fetches and packs the meshes into examples-style meshes/*.json with a LICENCE.md, and writes a build.mjs from the brain example. The delivered light page is one standalone HTML file with a WebGL canvas in the framed card: drag turns it, it opens anterior forward and superior up, each lobe is in its own tissue tone, hovering a part lights it and writes n · Name in the readout, arrows step the parts in key order, Q hides the names, and numbered tags sit on their own parts. The key under the card lists every part, every one of the nine (frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital lobes, insula, cerebellum, midbrain, pons, medulla oblongata) by number and name, generated from truth.mjs, and the caption cites BodyParts3D 4.0, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP and the fetch date. checkTruth passes, scripts/view-check.mjs prints view-check: ok, and the front, left and top were captured and read against the atlas before delivery.

evals.prompt: The hippocampus with the amygdala, fornix and parahippocampal gyrus around it, in 3D so I can see how they sit. Dark theme, one HTML file.
evals.expected_output: 3D route, BodyParts3D (human). atlas.mjs bp3d --find confirms hippocampus, amygdala, fornix of forebrain and parahippocampal gyrus; truth.mjs has four rows with those ids and the atlas's names, the fornix in the tract tone, the amygdala in the nucleus tone, the hippocampus in its own tone, the gyrus in the cortex tone. One dark standalone page: all four parts in the key by number and name, generated from the truth table; hover names each part; arrows step with the stepped part lit and the rest dimmed, never transparent; Q hides the names; the caption cites BodyParts3D and its licence. The response says what the atlas does not have: no human hippocampal subfields (CA fields, dentate gyrus) as meshes, and offers the mouse hippocampal formation from the Allen atlas as a second card or a drawn coronal section on the section route if the user wants the subfields. checkTruth passes and view-check prints ok.

evals.prompt: The brainstem as midbrain, pons and medulla, with the cerebellum behind it, for revision. One file I can open offline.
evals.expected_output: 3D route, BodyParts3D: midbrain, pons, medulla oblongata and cerebellum, four rows in truth.mjs with atlas ids and names, the three brainstem parts in the brainstem tone and the cerebellum in its own. The response says the figure takes minutes. One offline HTML page: the model opens in anatomical position with the cerebellum behind the brainstem, every part in the key by number and name, hover and arrows name them, Q hides the names, the caption cites BodyParts3D 4.0, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP and the fetch date. Names follow the atlas (medulla oblongata, not medulla) unless the user pasted a list, and the response says so. checkTruth passes, view-check prints ok, three captures were read against the atlas.

evals.prompt: Show me the thalamus and hypothalamus and where they sit under the cortex. Light theme.
evals.expected_output: 3D route, BodyParts3D. truth.mjs has the thalamus and hypothalamus in the nucleus tone, plus the context the user asked for as named parts the atlas has (for example the cerebral lobes or the whole brain as one mesh, and the brainstem), each with its atlas ids and names, so the two nuclei can be found under the cortex by stepping to them, which lights them and dims the rest. Every part in the figure, context included, is in the key by number and name; nothing is drawn by hand. One light standalone HTML file, hover names, arrows step, Q quiz, the caption cites BodyParts3D and its licence. The response says that parts are never made transparent, so the user steps or turns to see the nuclei, and asks before adding a drawn section if the user wants the thalamic nuclei, which the atlas does not have. checkTruth passes and view-check prints ok.

evals.prompt: Make me a figure of a pyramidal neuron with the three glial cell types around it, with every part labelled so I can test myself: soma, dendrites, axon hillock, axon, myelin sheath, nodes of Ranvier, axon terminals, astrocyte, oligodendrocyte, microglia. Dark theme, standalone HTML.
evals.expected_output: The response takes the section route and says why: no atlas has a neuron or its glia as meshes. It sizes it as a Figure (30-90 minutes). A dark standalone isometric page of a neuron on a stand with a truth.mjs listing the ten parts the user named verbatim, in the user's order, SOURCE.convention set to the user's list, and sources fetched only for borders and connections. The soma is a sphere or lathe, dendrites are routes that leave it tangent and branch at ball tees, the axon hillock tapers, the axon is one route with myelin collars gapping it and bare nodes between, terminals end on balls, and each glial cell is its own body whose processes end on something (the neuron, a collar, a capillary). One pin per part, every one of the ten parts in the key by number and name, generated from the truth table, quiz mode working (Q hides names, click reveals). checkTruth passes, --audit ends audit passed, line ends: 0, 4x close-ups of every end and collar in both themes were read.
